Waiting until you're "older" to seek help can actually work against you. The earlier you understand what's happening, the more options you have.

At Pluro Fertility and IVF, we treat every patient as an individual  not a statistic. Our specialists build personalised treatment plans based on your biology, your history, and your goals.
IVF is for anyone who needs it. Full stop.

Myth: Birth control pills cause infertility. 
This is one of the most common fertility misconceptions — and it stops women from making informed decisions about their reproductive health every single day.

The fact? There is no scientific evidence linking birth control pills to permanent infertility. Oral contraceptives temporarily suppress ovulation while you're on them. Once stopped, your natural cycle gradually resumes. For most women, fertility returns within a few months.

If you've been avoiding contraception out of fear or worrying about past pill use affecting your chances of conceiving  this is your clarity.

That said, if you've been trying to conceive for a while without success, the reason is unlikely to be your contraceptive history. Factors like age, PCOS, blocked fallopian tubes, low AMH, or male infertility are far more common causes worth investigating.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Based on my experience on 10th May 2021:

Since this is a new centre for vaccination opened last Friday by the BMC, there is not much clarity/information available online. This centre is currently open for 18-44 age group, and primarily Covaxin (subject to availability). There is not much clarity about walk-ins, better to call and confirm as they were only accepting appointments via CoWIN when I visited. Location specified on Google Maps is accurate.

An extremely well-maintained, organized vaccination centre with professional service by the officials. There are 3-4 levels of screenings and procedures before you get vaccinated, which is managed brilliantly. Prefer a morning slot if possible, reach the centre by 8:30am. They allow entry in an orderly manner at sharp 9am if everything goes well.

First level: General health details. Please provide accurate answers to the questions about any health conditions, symptoms, etc.

Second level: This is where you receive your token/card from BMC with all your details, verified with your appointment online. They will also specify booth/token number. After this, proceed to the waiting zone, which has an LED indicator to show the current token ongoing.

Third level: Once your token number is displayed, proceed to your booth (there are 2 booths which function simultaneously) and wait for the previous person to vacate. Get vaccinated, follow all the necessary instructions specified by the vaccinating doctor, and proceed towards the observation zone.

Fourth level: Wait patiently for 30 minutes. Please do not insist to leave any earlier, just to make sure there are no side effects. Once your 30-minute cooldown is complete, you can show your token/card and collect your vaccination certificate.

The entire process, takes just about 30-40 minutes, thanks to the dedicated staff (this was specifically for the morning slot 9-11am, your experience may vary depending on the time of the day).
Kindly co-operate with the officials, and please be patient, they are way more stressed than us, we need to go through this process just once per dose. Overall, it was totally worth 40 minutes of my travel to this centre.

featured_reviews.name: Vivek Av
featured_reviews.review_text:
I was admitted to Sapna Hospital for malaria and stayed for 4 days.
It was extremely concerning to see mosquito issues inside the ward while being treated for a mosquito-borne illness. A repellent machine was only provided after repeated complaints.
Hygiene standards were disappointing. I noticed what appeared to be blood stains in saline lines, a dustbin near my bed containing vomit that was not cleared promptly, and an ice pad provided to me that had visible hair on it. Used gloves were also left openly near patient beds instead of being disposed of immediately and bed bugs.
These are basic infection-control practices that should be strictly maintained in any hospital.
Staff behavior at times felt indifferent, and response seemed noticeably quicker when services involved billing.
For a bill of approximately ₹30,000 in just 3 days, I expected a much higher standard of cleanliness, monitoring, and patient care.
I hope the management takes this feedback seriously and improves hygiene control and patient handling to ensure patient safety.
